**CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY-CLIENT WORK PRODUCT** Prepared at the direction of outside counsel, Westbrook Callahan LLP, for use in connection with the development of the Antelope Plateau Wind Project. This memorandum is protected by the attorney-client privilege and work product doctrine.

**MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** Jordan Hale, Vice President of Land & Development, Ridgeline Wind Holdings LLC

**FROM:** Kevin Obermeyer, Trailhead Land Services LLC, Pendleton, Oregon

**DATE:** January 8, 2025

**RE:** Millard Family Revocable Trust Parcels --- Strategic Assessment and Project Timeline Considerations, Antelope Plateau Wind Project

**[1. Executive Summary]{.underline}**

This memorandum summarizes the strategic importance of the three Millard Family Revocable Trust parcels --- totaling approximately 4,200 acres in Gilliam County, Oregon --- to the Antelope Plateau Wind Project (300 MW nameplate capacity). The Land Option and Lease Agreement governing these parcels was executed on December 18, 2024, between Ridgeline Wind Holdings LLC and The Millard Family Revocable Trust (Eleanor Millard, Trustee).

The Millard parcels are among the most critical parcels in the project footprint. They contain three of the five highest-capacity turbine locations identified in the micrositing study and the **only viable substation interconnection site** for the project. Ridgeline currently controls approximately 13,800 acres across 14 executed land agreements; the addition of the Millard parcels brings total controlled acreage to approximately 18,000 acres.

This memo addresses: (1) parcel descriptions and suitability, (2) strategic importance to the project layout, (3) key agreement terms relevant to development planning, and (4) project timeline milestones, including a critical scheduling observation regarding the overlap between the option extension notice deadline and the target commercial operation date. The project holds BPA interconnection queue position Q-2024-0287, and development scheduling is anchored to that queue position.

**[2. Parcel Descriptions and Suitability]{.underline}**

**Parcel A: Tax Lot 200, Map No. 3S-21E-12 --- Approximately 1,840 Acres**

Parcel A is located in the northwestern portion of the project area. The terrain consists of gently rolling plateau with predominant grass and rangeland cover, at elevations ranging from approximately 2,400 to 2,750 feet. Current use includes dryland wheat rotation and cattle grazing. The landowner, Eleanor Millard (age 74), operates a cattle ranch on the property; the successor trustee under the trust instrument is her son, Douglas Millard (age 51).

Parcel A contains the only location identified as viable for the project\'s interconnection substation, based on proximity to the existing BPA transmission corridor and suitable topography for substation construction. The executed agreement includes a transmission easement --- a 150-foot-wide corridor extending approximately 2.3 miles across Parcel A --- for the interconnection line. Parcel A also hosts one of the three high-capacity turbine locations situated on Millard land.

My site inspection confirmed minimal slope constraints within the substation footprint area, no identified wetlands, and adequate soil bearing capacity based on preliminary geotechnical review.

**Parcel B: Tax Lot 400, Map No. 3S-22E-07 --- Approximately 1,620 Acres**

Parcel B is located east of Parcel A, separated by approximately 1.5 miles. The terrain is open plateau, predominantly rangeland with scattered dryland wheat fields. This parcel hosts one of the three high-capacity turbine locations on Millard land and exhibits a strong and consistent wind resource based on preliminary anemometer data. One of the two existing meteorological towers in the project area is located on this parcel. Access to Parcel B will require construction of approximately 3.2 miles of new access road (24-foot width, aggregate surface, consistent with agreement specifications).

**Parcel C: Tax Lot 150, Map No. 3S-22E-18 --- Approximately 740 Acres**

Parcel C is the smallest of the three parcels, located southeast of Parcel B. It hosts one of the three high-capacity turbine locations --- specifically, the location with the single highest projected capacity factor in the entire micrositing study, estimated at approximately 42% net capacity factor. The terrain is suitable for turbine construction, though a minor drainage feature in the southern portion of the parcel will need to be avoided during road layout. Current use is primarily cattle grazing.

**Summary.** Total acreage across the three parcels: 1,840 + 1,620 + 740 = **4,200 acres**. The trust address of record is 38710 Bickleton Highway, Condon, OR 97823.

**[3. Strategic Importance to Antelope Plateau Wind Project]{.underline}**

**Substation Interconnection --- No Alternative.** The interconnection substation location on Parcel A is the only viable site identified in the interconnection study submitted to BPA under queue position Q-2024-0287. Loss of this parcel would require a new interconnection study, likely a new queue position, and could delay the project by two to three years --- or render it unviable entirely.

**High-Capacity Turbine Locations.** The micrositing study identified five locations across the approximately 18,000-acre project footprint with projected net capacity factors exceeding 38%. Three of these five are on Millard Trust land --- one each on Parcels A, B, and C. The loss of these three positions would reduce projected annual energy production by an estimated 12--15%, materially impacting project economics and potentially jeopardizing the pro forma relied upon by Highline Capital Group in the project financing.

**Collection System Routing.** Parcels A and B are positioned such that the underground collection system from the eastern and central turbine strings must cross Millard land to reach the substation. Without these parcels, collection routing alternatives would add significant cost and complexity.

**Minimum Turbine Assumption.** The agreement assumes a minimum of 35 turbines across the three Millard parcels, reflecting the anticipated density based on the micrositing layout. This is a significant concentration --- approximately 35 out of an estimated project-wide total of 100 to 120 turbines, depending on final turbine model selection for 300 MW nameplate.

In summary, the Millard Trust parcels are not merely important --- they are **indispensable** to the Antelope Plateau project as currently designed. Any lapse or loss of rights to these parcels would constitute a critical project risk event.

**[4. Key Agreement Terms Relevant to Development Planning]{.underline}**

The following is a brief summary of the executed agreement terms most relevant to development scheduling and field operations. This is not a full legal review; outside counsel at Westbrook Callahan LLP is conducting a comprehensive review of the agreement.

**Option Period.** The initial option term is three years, running from December 18, 2024 through December 18, 2027, with two one-year extensions at Ridgeline\'s election (maximum term through December 18, 2029). Option payments are structured as follows: Years 1--2 at \$18.00 per acre (\$75,600 per year); Year 3 at \$20.00 per acre (\$84,000); Extension Year 4 at \$22.00 per acre (\$92,400); Extension Year 5 at \$24.00 per acre (\$100,800). Total maximum option payments over five years: \$428,400.

**Extension Notice Requirement.** Written notice of extension must be delivered not less than 90 days before expiration of the then-current term.

**Pre-Development Access.** Ridgeline may conduct environmental, geotechnical, and wind monitoring studies during the option period. Up to four meteorological towers may be installed without additional compensation. Entry requires 72 hours\' advance notice, reduced to 24 hours for met tower maintenance.

**Lease Term.** Thirty years from COD, with one 20-year renewal at Ridgeline\'s election (total potential term of 50 years).

**Construction Coordination.** Turbine and road placement must minimize interference with ranching operations, including cattle grazing and dryland wheat cultivation. Fencing damaged during construction must be repaired within 10 business days. Turbine setback is 1,500 feet from any occupied dwelling existing as of the execution date. Access roads must be a minimum of 24 feet in width with an aggregate surface.

**Crop and Grazing Damage.** A one-time payment of \$175 per acre applies for permanently disturbed acres, estimated at 280 acres (\$49,000 total).

Title work is being coordinated through Columbia Basin Title & Escrow in The Dalles. Bridger Appraisal & Consulting was referenced in the agreement in connection with property valuation matters.

**[5. Project Timeline Milestones and Critical Scheduling Observation]{.underline}**

**5.1 Key Milestones**

The following timeline reflects my understanding of anticipated project milestones based on discussions with Jordan Hale and the Ridgeline development team:

> • **Q1 2025:** Complete Phase 1 environmental surveys on Millard parcels; install two additional meteorological towers on Parcels B and C.
>
> • **Q2--Q3 2025:** Finalize micrositing layout; submit Gilliam County conditional use permit application.
>
> • **Q4 2025 -- Q1 2026:** Obtain conditional use permit; complete geotechnical investigations.
>
> • **Q2 2026:** Financial close with Highline Capital Group (project finance lender, lead arranger). Lender\'s counsel Stratton Whitaker LLP (Marcus Reyes) will conduct due diligence on all land agreements.
>
> • **Q3 2026:** Begin road construction and foundation work.
>
> • **Q1--Q3 2027:** Turbine delivery and erection; substation construction on Parcel A.
>
> • **Q4 2027:** Target commercial operation date (COD). Commissioning and grid synchronization via BPA interconnection (queue Q-2024-0287).

**5.2 Critical Timing Overlap --- Option Extension Deadline vs. COD**

I want to call particular attention to a scheduling overlap that presents a meaningful commercial risk for Ridgeline.

**The facts are as follows.** The initial option period expires **December 18, 2027**. The first extension election (Year 3 to Year 4) requires written notice **not less than 90 days** before expiration of the initial term --- meaning the deadline for the first extension notice is **September 20, 2027**. The target COD is **Q4 2027**, which Ridgeline has generally described as the October through December 2027 timeframe.

**The timing overlap.** The September 20, 2027 extension notice deadline falls in the same quarter as the anticipated COD. As of September 20, 2027, Ridgeline will likely be in the final stages of commissioning but may not yet have achieved COD.

**Scenario A --- Project on track for Q4 2027 COD.** Ridgeline\'s intent would be to exercise the option and convert to the lease upon achieving COD. However, if COD has not yet occurred by September 20, Ridgeline faces uncertainty. If Ridgeline does *not* send the extension notice by September 20 --- because it expects to achieve COD before December 18 --- but then COD slips past December 18, the option would expire without being extended and without being exercised. Ridgeline could lose all rights to the Millard parcels, and with them, the substation site and three high-capacity turbine locations. Given the analysis in Section 3 above, this would effectively end the Antelope Plateau project.

**Scenario B --- Project delayed.** If delays push COD into 2028, Ridgeline would need to extend the option. The extension notice must be sent by September 20, 2027. This is manageable if the delay is identified well in advance, but construction schedules for wind projects are notoriously volatile in the final months --- weather events, turbine delivery delays, and BPA interconnection scheduling can each independently push COD by weeks or months.

**Protective measure --- send extension notice regardless.** My recommendation is that Ridgeline should plan to deliver the extension notice by September 20, 2027 as a protective measure in all scenarios, even if COD is firmly expected before year-end. The question that follows is whether the agreement\'s option exercise mechanism allows Ridgeline to exercise the option and convert to the lease even after an extension notice has been sent --- that is, does exercising the option supersede and terminate the extension? I would flag this question for review by Sarah Fong at Westbrook Callahan LLP.

On the financial side, sending the extension notice would trigger the Year 4 option payment of \$22.00 per acre × 4,200 acres = \$92,400. This is a relatively modest cost compared to the risk of losing the parcels, but Ridgeline should confirm with counsel whether the extension payment obligation arises only if the extension actually takes effect --- that is, if the option is exercised and the lease commences before the extension period begins, does Ridgeline still owe the Year 4 option payment?

**In summary**, this timing overlap creates a narrow window in which Ridgeline must make a consequential decision with imperfect information about project completion timing. The development team and outside counsel should calendar the September 20, 2027 deadline immediately and develop a decision protocol well in advance of that date.

**[6. Recommendations and Next Steps]{.underline}**

1\. **Calendar the September 20, 2027 extension notice deadline.** This is the single most time-sensitive action item arising from this assessment. I recommend adding this date to the project master schedule and assigning a responsible party. I suggest Jordan Hale as the primary responsible party with backup notification to outside counsel Sarah Fong at Westbrook Callahan LLP.

2\. **Coordinate with outside counsel** on whether the agreement permits option exercise after an extension notice has been delivered, and whether Year 4 option payments can be avoided if COD occurs before December 18, 2027. This should be flagged for Westbrook Callahan LLP\'s comprehensive agreement review.

3\. **Proceed with meteorological tower installations** on Parcels B and C in Q1 2025 as planned. Coordinate with Eleanor Millard (or Douglas Millard as successor trustee) per the 72-hour advance notice requirement in the agreement.

4\. **Initiate preliminary substation design** for the Parcel A interconnection site to support Gilliam County permitting and BPA interconnection engineering.

5\. **Support lender due diligence.** Highline Capital Group and their counsel at Stratton Whitaker LLP (Marcus Reyes) will require full copies of the executed agreement and recorded memorandum. Coordinate with Columbia Basin Title & Escrow to ensure the memorandum of agreement is recorded promptly in Gilliam County.

6\. **Maintain the landowner relationship.** Eleanor Millard has been a cooperative and engaged counterparty throughout the negotiation process. Given her age (74) and the long-term nature of the agreement, I recommend periodic check-ins and clear communication regarding construction timing and potential impacts on ranching operations. Douglas Millard should be included in all substantive communications in his capacity as successor trustee.

Trailhead Land Services remains available to assist with any field coordination, access logistics, or landowner relations as the project moves forward.

Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any questions or if additional information is needed.

Kevin Obermeyer Trailhead Land Services LLC Pendleton, Oregon (541) 555-0173 kobermeyer@trailheadland.com

39	**[II.A. Option Duration and Extensions]{.underline}**
40	
41	The option period secures Ridgeline\'s exclusive right to develop wind energy facilities on the landowner\'s property before Ridgeline commits to the full lease term. The option period must be long enough to allow Ridgeline to complete all pre-development activities --- including wind resource assessment, environmental permitting, interconnection studies, and project financing --- while preserving Ridgeline\'s flexibility to terminate if the project does not advance.
42	
43	**Preferred Initial Option Period:** Three (3) years from the effective date of the agreement.
44	
45	**Extensions:** Two (2) extension periods of one (1) year each, exercisable at Ridgeline\'s sole election. The maximum total option period, including both extensions, is five (5) years from the effective date.
46	
47	**Extension Notice Requirement:** Ridgeline must deliver written notice of its election to extend the option period no less than ninety (90) days prior to the expiration of the then-current option term. Failure to timely deliver the extension notice results in the option lapsing at the end of the then-current term.
48	
49	**Guidance Note for Land Agents:** The 90-day advance notice requirement creates a critical decision point well in advance of option expiration. Land agents should carefully calendar all extension notice deadlines at the time of agreement execution. For the Antelope Plateau Wind Project, with a target COD of Q4 2027 and initial option expiration dates for many agreements falling in the December 2027 timeframe (e.g., December 18, 2027 for early-executed agreements), the extension notice deadline for the Year 3-to-Year 4 extension would fall approximately September 20, 2027 --- potentially before Ridgeline has clarity on whether COD will be achieved on schedule. In these circumstances, Ridgeline may face a decision on whether to extend (and incur additional option payments) before it knows whether the option will be exercised. **Land agents should flag this timing overlap to Jordan Hale and legal counsel in any agreement where the option expiration date falls within six (6) months of the expected COD so that Ridgeline can plan its exercise and extension strategy accordingly.** This is particularly important for parcels that are critical to the project layout, such as parcels designated for substation sites, high-capacity turbine clusters, or transmission corridor routes. Early coordination between the land team, development team, and legal counsel will be essential to managing these overlapping deadlines.
50	
51	**Option Exercise:** Exercise of the option (i.e., conversion of the option into a full lease) must be by written notice from Ridgeline to the landowner, effective upon delivery in accordance with the notice provisions of the agreement. No specific form of exercise notice is required, but written notice must clearly state Ridgeline\'s intent to exercise the option and commence the lease term.

91	**[III.B. Rent Structure --- Calculation Methodology]{.underline}**
92	
93	Ridgeline\'s standard rent structure uses a \"greater-of\" mechanism designed to ensure that the landowner benefits from both a guaranteed minimum payment and the upside potential of electricity production. The structure consists of two alternative prongs; the landowner receives whichever amount is greater in any given payment period.
94	
95	**Prong (a): Base Rent + Capacity Payment**
96	
97	> • **Base Rent:** \$1,000--\$1,500 per turbine installed on the leased premises per year. The agreement should specify a negotiated minimum turbine count (typically 25--40 turbines, depending on parcel size and project layout) to provide the landowner with a guaranteed minimum base rent regardless of the actual number of turbines installed.
98	>
99	> • **Capacity Payment:** \$4,000--\$5,500 per megawatt (MW) of nameplate capacity of turbines installed on the leased premises per year. This payment scales with the generation capacity of the turbines placed on the parcel and provides additional compensation beyond the per-turbine base rent.
100	
101	**Prong (b): Production Royalty**
102	
103	> • 3.0%--4.0% of gross revenue from the sale of electricity generated by turbines located on the leased premises. \"Gross revenue\" should be defined to include energy payments, capacity payments, and renewable energy credit (REC) revenues attributable to turbines on the parcel.
104	
105	**Rent Determination:** The landowner receives the **GREATER of** Prong (a) or Prong (b) in any given year. Annual reconciliation is performed within ninety (90) days after the end of each calendar year, with a true-up payment to the landowner if the production royalty prong exceeds the sum of base rent and capacity payments already paid.
106	
107	**Substation Hosting Fee:**
108	
109	Where a landowner\'s parcel hosts a project substation, collector substation, or interconnection facility, a flat annual Substation Hosting Fee is payable to the landowner. The preferred range is **\$25,000--\$40,000 per year**, depending on the size and voltage class of the facility and the extent of the land disturbance.
110	
111	**CRITICAL --- The Substation Hosting Fee is a standalone payment and must be stated as payable \"in addition to\" whichever prong of the greater-of calculation applies.** The Substation Hosting Fee must NOT be folded into either Prong (a) or Prong (b). Drafters and reviewing attorneys must ensure that the agreement explicitly states language substantially similar to the following:
112	
113	> *\"In addition to the Annual Rent calculated under Section \[X\], Developer shall pay Landowner the Substation Hosting Fee as set forth in Section \[Y\], which fee shall be payable regardless of whether Annual Rent is determined under Prong (a) or Prong (b) of the rent calculation and shall not be included in either prong for purposes of the greater-of comparison.\"*
114	
115	**Rationale:** The Substation Hosting Fee compensates the landowner for a distinct and incremental land use --- hosting high-voltage electrical equipment, increased heavy vehicle traffic, visual and noise impact from transformers and switching gear, and potential electromagnetic field exposure --- that is separate from and additional to the use of the parcel for wind turbine siting. If the Substation Hosting Fee is not clearly separated from the greater-of calculation, disputes may arise as to whether the fee is subsumed within the annual rent comparison, potentially reducing total landowner compensation in years when the production royalty prong exceeds the fixed-payment prong. This ambiguity has been a source of confusion in prior Ridgeline negotiations and must be resolved unambiguously in every agreement where a substation or interconnection facility is sited on a landowner\'s parcel.
116	
117	**[III.C. Crop/Grazing Damage Payments]{.underline}**
118	
119	A one-time crop and grazing damage payment of **\$150--\$200 per acre** is payable for each acre permanently disturbed during the construction phase. \"Permanently disturbed\" means acreage occupied by turbine foundations, access roads, laydown areas, substations, and other project facilities that are not restored to agricultural use following construction.
120	
121	Payment is due within thirty (30) days of completion of construction activities on the affected acreage, as confirmed by Ridgeline\'s construction manager. The landowner retains the right to farm, graze, and conduct agricultural operations on all areas of the property not occupied by project facilities, subject to reasonable safety setbacks around turbine towers and electrical equipment.
122	
123	**[III.D. Escalation]{.underline}**
124	
125	**Preferred Escalator:** All fixed payments --- including base rent (per turbine), capacity payment (per MW), and Substation Hosting Fee --- escalate at a rate of **2.0% per year, compounding annually**, commencing on the third (3rd) anniversary of COD.
126	
127	**Escalator Commencement:** The escalator does not apply during the first three (3) years of the lease term. Beginning on the third anniversary of COD, the escalator applies to the fixed payment amounts in effect as of the immediately preceding year.
128	
129	**Note on Production Royalty:** The production royalty percentage under Prong (b) is **not** subject to escalation, because the royalty inherently adjusts with changes in electricity market prices and generation output. However, land agents should be aware that in years when the production royalty prong exceeds the escalated fixed-payment prong, the landowner receives no benefit from the escalation mechanism. In such years, the landowner\'s total compensation is determined solely by the royalty percentage applied to gross revenue. Consider on a case-by-case basis whether a royalty floor escalation mechanism (i.e., a minimum annual rent that escalates regardless of the greater-of comparison) is warranted to address this concern.
130	
131	**Acceptable Alternative:** Some executed Ridgeline agreements apply the 2.0% escalator to \"all payments including a royalty floor.\" This formulation establishes a minimum annual rent that escalates over time, ensuring the landowner receives escalation benefits even in high-royalty years. This alternative is acceptable but not required by the Playbook.

193	**[VI. Assignment and Transfer Provisions]{.underline}**
194	
195	**[VI.A. Ridgeline Assignment Rights]{.underline}**
196	
197	**Must-Have:** Ridgeline may freely assign the agreement, in whole or in part, to any **affiliate** without the landowner\'s consent. An \"affiliate\" is defined as any entity that, directly or indirectly, controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with Ridgeline Wind Holdings LLC or Cascade Renewables Inc. \"Control\" means the ownership of fifty percent (50%) or more of the voting equity interests of an entity or the power to direct the management and policies of an entity.
198	
199	**Assignment to Non-Affiliates:** Assignment to a non-affiliate entity requires the landowner\'s prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. The landowner shall respond to an assignment consent request within thirty (30) days of receipt; failure to respond within such period is deemed consent.
200	
201	**Qualified Transferee Provision:** Ridgeline\'s preferred form includes a \"Qualified Transferee\" carve-out that operates as an exception to the non-affiliate consent requirement. Under this provision, assignment to any entity meeting both of the following criteria is deemed a \"Qualified Transfer\" and does not require landowner consent:
202	
203	> \(a\) The transferee has a net worth of at least **\$50 million** (determined in accordance with GAAP based on the transferee\'s most recent audited financial statements); and
204	>
205	> \(b\) The transferee (or its affiliates) has experience operating wind energy projects with an aggregate nameplate capacity of at least **200 MW**.
206	
207	**Guidance for Land Agents:** The Qualified Transferee thresholds are set at levels designed to facilitate project sales, tax equity transactions, and financing-related assignments while ensuring that the project is transferred only to creditworthy and experienced operators. Land agents should be aware that these thresholds are relatively modest by current renewable energy industry standards --- most mid-size and large wind developers, infrastructure funds, yieldcos, and regulated utilities will readily meet both criteria. If a landowner specifically negotiates for consent rights over assignment, the Qualified Transferee carve-out may substantially limit the practical scope of that consent right, because the vast majority of likely assignees will qualify as Qualified Transferees. In sensitive negotiations --- for example, where the landowner is a family trust, a long-established ranching operation, or an individual with strong attachment to the identity of the counterparty --- consider whether higher thresholds (e.g., \$100 million net worth, 500 MW experience) would be more appropriate to give the consent right meaningful practical effect. However, the current thresholds of \$50 million and 200 MW are acceptable and preferred for speed of execution, and they have been accepted by Highline Capital Group and its counsel as consistent with project finance requirements.

223	**[VII. Decommissioning and Removal]{.underline}**
224	
225	**[VII.A. Decommissioning Obligations]{.underline}**
226	
227	Upon expiration or earlier termination of the lease, or upon abandonment of the project, Ridgeline must decommission and remove all project facilities from the property within **eighteen (18) months** after the triggering event. Decommissioning includes the removal of all turbine components (towers, nacelles, rotors, foundations to a depth of four feet below grade), electrical collection lines, substation equipment, access roads (unless the landowner elects in writing to retain roads), and all other Ridgeline-owned improvements.
228	
229	**Restoration Standard:** Following removal, the property must be restored to a condition **substantially similar to the condition that existed prior to construction and suitable for agricultural use**, including regrading, reseeding, and decompaction of soils as necessary.
230	
231	**Abandonment Definition:** The project, or any individual turbine, is deemed \"abandoned\" if it has not generated electricity for a period of **twenty-four (24) consecutive months**, excluding any period during which non-generation is attributable to (i) force majeure events, (ii) scheduled maintenance or equipment upgrades, or (iii) curtailment directed by the grid operator or balancing authority.
232	
233	**[VII.B. Decommissioning Security --- Timing and Amount]{.underline}**
234	
235	**MUST-HAVE (Ridgeline Preferred Position):** Ridgeline must post decommissioning security --- in the form of a surety bond or an irrevocable standby letter of credit --- **no later than the Commercial Operation Date (COD).**
236	
237	**Preferred Amount:** \$40,000--\$50,000 per turbine installed on the property. The specific amount for each agreement should be validated by an independent decommissioning cost estimate prepared by Bridger Appraisal & Consulting or another qualified firm with experience in wind energy decommissioning cost assessment.
238	
239	**Acceptable Surety Providers:** Pineridge Surety Co. or any surety company holding an A.M. Best financial strength rating of \"A\" (Excellent) or better. As an alternative to a surety bond, Ridgeline may post an irrevocable standby letter of credit issued by a financial institution with an investment-grade credit rating (BBB- or higher from S&P, or Baa3 or higher from Moody\'s).
240	
241	**Timing Rationale:** Decommissioning security must be in place from COD to protect the landowner and to satisfy the requirements of Ridgeline\'s project finance lenders. Highline Capital Group and its counsel, Stratton Whitaker LLP, have consistently required evidence of decommissioning security as either a condition to credit facility closing or a post-closing covenant requiring posting within a specified period after COD. Deferring the security posting obligation to a later date --- for example, the 10th or 15th anniversary of COD --- creates an unacceptable gap during which neither the landowner nor the project lender has financial assurance that the cost of facility removal will be borne by Ridgeline (or its surety). If Ridgeline were to become insolvent, undergo a change of control, or abandon the project before the deferred posting date, the landowner would bear the full cost of decommissioning, which can exceed \$45,000 per turbine based on current industry estimates. For a parcel hosting 8--12 turbines, the total decommissioning liability could range from \$360,000 to \$540,000 or more --- a sum that would impose severe financial hardship on most agricultural landowners. This risk has been identified and raised by project finance lenders in due diligence on prior Ridgeline transactions, and it is a known concern of county planning authorities in Oregon.
242	
243	**Negotiation Note:** Some landowners will accept a posting date of COD + 5 years as a compromise, particularly where Ridgeline agrees to a higher security amount or automatic inflation adjustment. This compromise is acceptable, though COD posting remains preferred. Posting later than the 10th anniversary of COD is **not recommended** and requires prior written approval from Jordan Hale, VP of Land & Development, and Ridgeline\'s General Counsel. Any executed agreement in which the decommissioning security posting obligation is deferred beyond COD + 10 years should be flagged as a deviation from the Playbook standard and documented in the deviation tracker described in Section XIII.

275	**Ridgeline\'s Indemnification of Landowner:** Ridgeline shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the landowner and the landowner\'s heirs, successors, assigns, trustees, and beneficiaries from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising out of or related to Ridgeline\'s construction, operation, maintenance, or decommissioning activities on the property, **except** to the extent that such claims are caused by the landowner\'s gross negligence or willful misconduct.

281	**Guidance Note:** Land agents and counsel should be aware that a 3-year survival period, while standard in Ridgeline\'s form, may be shorter than certain applicable Oregon statutes of limitation. Under ORS 12.110, the statute of limitations for personal injury actions is two (2) years from the date of discovery of the injury. A 3-year indemnification survival period may therefore expire before the landowner\'s underlying cause of action is time-barred, leaving the landowner without contractual indemnification protection during a portion of the limitations period. 287	**Monetary Defaults:** A monetary default (failure to pay option consideration, rent, or any other amounts due under the agreement) is subject to a cure period of **sixty (60) days** from the date of written notice from the non-defaulting party specifying the nature and amount of the monetary default.
288	
289	**Non-Monetary Defaults:** A non-monetary default (breach of any covenant, representation, or obligation other than a payment obligation) is subject to a cure period of **ninety (90) days** from the date of written notice. If the nature of the non-monetary default is such that it cannot reasonably be cured within ninety (90) days, the cure period is automatically extended to **one hundred eighty (180) days**, provided that the defaulting party is diligently pursuing cure and provides periodic written progress reports to the non-defaulting party.
290	
291	**[X.B. Specific Performance and Remedies]{.underline}**
292	
293	**Must-Have for Ridgeline:** Ridgeline must have the contractual right to seek **specific performance** against the landowner in the event of a landowner default or attempted breach, including but not limited to an attempted sale, conveyance, or encumbrance of the property in violation of the agreement, a refusal to grant access in accordance with the agreement\'s terms, or an attempt to terminate the agreement without contractual basis. This remedy is critical because wind energy project parcels are unique --- each parcel is selected based on site-specific wind resource data, micrositing studies, avian and environmental assessments, and interconnection feasibility analyses. The loss of a key parcel --- especially one designated to host a project substation, a concentration of high-capacity turbine locations, or a critical segment of the electrical collection system or transmission corridor --- could jeopardize the viability of the entire Antelope Plateau Wind Project. Monetary damages alone are inadequate to compensate Ridgeline for the loss of development rights on a parcel whose characteristics cannot be replicated on alternative land.
294	
295	**Landowner\'s Remedies:** Ridgeline\'s preferred position is that the landowner\'s exclusive remedy for a Ridgeline default is **monetary damages** --- i.e., the landowner does not have the right to seek specific performance compelling Ridgeline to construct, operate, or continue operating the wind energy project. **Rationale:** Specific performance compelling Ridgeline to construct or operate a multi-hundred-million-dollar wind energy facility would be impractical and unduly burdensome. The exercise of development rights is a business decision that depends on factors beyond the scope of any single land agreement --- including power purchase agreement terms, interconnection availability, equipment pricing, and capital market conditions. Monetary damages (including lost rent and option payments) adequately compensate the landowner for the economic value of the development rights.
296	
297	**Guidance Note (Risk Acknowledgment):** Land agents and counsel should be aware that this asymmetric remedy structure --- specific performance available to Ridgeline but not to the landowner --- may face scrutiny in certain contexts, particularly when the landowner is an unsophisticated individual, an elderly person, or a trust fiduciary acting on behalf of beneficiaries with limited business experience. In Oregon, courts retain equitable discretion to decline enforcement of specific performance provisions or limitation-of-remedy clauses that are deemed unconscionable, particularly where there is a significant disparity in bargaining power between the parties. If a landowner or the landowner\'s counsel raises this issue during negotiations, consider the following alternatives: (a) offering a **mutual specific performance** right, under which both parties may seek specific performance for the other\'s breach (this is acceptable but not preferred); or (b) enhancing the monetary damages available to the landowner, such as through a **liquidated damages** provision establishing a predetermined payment amount in the event of Ridgeline\'s early termination or default. **Do not concede this point without consulting Westbrook Callahan LLP (Sarah Fong, Partner).**
298	
299	**[X.C. Arbitration]{.underline}**
300	
301	**Disputes Exceeding \$100,000:** Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to the agreement in which the amount in controversy exceeds \$100,000 shall be resolved by **binding arbitration** administered by the American Arbitration Association (AAA) under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, before a single arbitrator with experience in energy or real property matters. The arbitration shall be held in Portland, Oregon, unless the parties agree otherwise.
302	
303	**Disputes at or Below \$100,000:** Disputes involving amounts of \$100,000 or less may be brought in the appropriate state court of competent jurisdiction. Ridgeline\'s preferred venue is the **Circuit Court of Gilliam County, Oregon**, for all Oregon-sited project agreements. Both parties consent to personal jurisdiction and venue in Gilliam County for purposes of such disputes.
304	
305	**[XI. Most-Favored-Nations (MFN) Provisions]{.underline}**
306	
307	**Classification: PREFERRED BUT OPTIONAL**
308	
309	Ridgeline\'s standard form agreement does **not** include a Most-Favored-Nations clause. However, an MFN clause is a common landowner request and has become an increasingly standard provision in the wind energy industry, particularly in projects involving multiple adjoining or nearby landowners.
310	
311	**Definition:** An MFN clause entitles the landowner to receive commercial terms --- including option rates, lease rent, and royalty percentages --- at least as favorable as those offered to other landowners participating in the same project. If Ridgeline subsequently enters into a land agreement with another landowner on the same project on more favorable terms, the MFN clause obligates Ridgeline to adjust the original landowner\'s terms to match.
312	
313	**Ridgeline\'s Position:** MFN clauses are preferred but not required. They should be offered proactively in negotiations where the landowner is likely to compare terms with neighboring landowners --- a common dynamic in tight-knit rural communities such as those in Gilliam County, where landowners frequently communicate with one another about lease terms. Where an MFN clause is included, it should be narrowly scoped:
314	
315	> • The MFN applies only to **per-acre option rates, base rent per turbine, capacity payment per MW, and production royalty percentages.**
316	>
317	> • The MFN does **not** apply to Substation Hosting Fees, one-time payments (crop/grazing damage), or project-specific accommodations negotiated to address unique parcel characteristics (e.g., visual screening, well relocation, irrigation pivot relocation).
318	>
319	> • The MFN comparison is limited to agreements **executed after the effective date** of the subject agreement. It does not apply retroactively to agreements executed before the subject agreement.
320	
321	Where an MFN clause is **not** included, land agents should document the rationale in the negotiation file --- for example, that the landowner did not request an MFN clause, that parcel characteristics justify different economics, or that the landowner\'s agreement was among the last to be executed (reducing the likelihood of subsequently more favorable terms).
322	
323	**Risk of Omission:** In projects involving multiple landowners --- the Antelope Plateau Wind Project involves fourteen (14) or more executed and pending land agreements --- the absence of an MFN clause may become a source of significant landowner dissatisfaction if the landowner later discovers that a neighboring participant received more favorable commercial terms. This can lead to relationship deterioration, political opposition to the project in county land use proceedings, or demands for renegotiation that create project delay and additional cost. In prior Ridgeline projects, the absence of MFN protections in certain agreements contributed to landowner grievances that required substantial management attention to resolve. Land agents should weigh these risks carefully when advising on whether to include or omit an MFN clause in any given negotiation.
324	
325	**[XII. Tax, Recording, and Miscellaneous Provisions]{.underline}**
326	
327	**[XII.A. Tax Responsibilities]{.underline}**
328	
329	**Real Property Taxes on Underlying Land:** The landowner is solely responsible for the payment of all real property taxes, assessments, and levies on the underlying land, consistent with the landowner\'s obligations as fee owner of the property.
330	
331	**Taxes on Ridgeline\'s Improvements:** Ridgeline is solely responsible for the payment of all taxes, assessments, and levies imposed on Ridgeline\'s improvements and personal property located on the premises, including wind turbines, electrical equipment, substations, and related facilities. All of Ridgeline\'s improvements are and shall remain the **personal property** of Ridgeline and shall not be deemed fixtures or improvements to the real property for purposes of property tax assessment or for any other purpose.
332	
333	**[XII.B. Recording]{.underline}**
334	
335	A **memorandum of the agreement** --- not the full agreement itself --- shall be recorded in the land records of the county in which the property is located. The memorandum form should be attached as **Exhibit B** to the agreement and should be executed by both parties simultaneously with the execution of the agreement.
336	
337	Coordinate all recording activities with **Columbia Basin Title & Escrow**, 315 East Second Street, The Dalles, OR 97058. Ensure that the memorandum contains a legally sufficient property description (metes and bounds or tax lot references) and identifies all material encumbrances and rights granted under the agreement, including the option, lease, easements, and right of first refusal. The memorandum should reference the agreement by its effective date and the parties\' names but should not disclose specific financial terms (option rates, rent amounts, royalty percentages).
338	
339	**[XII.C. Confidentiality]{.underline}**
340	
341	The terms and conditions of the agreement are confidential, and neither party shall disclose the specific financial or commercial terms to any third party except:
342	
343	> • As required by law, regulation, or order of a court or governmental authority;
344	>
345	> • To Ridgeline\'s project finance lenders (Highline Capital Group) and their counsel (Stratton Whitaker LLP) in connection with financing due diligence and loan documentation;
346	>
347	> • To Ridgeline\'s outside counsel (Westbrook Callahan LLP), land agents (Trailhead Land Services LLC), and appraisers (Bridger Appraisal & Consulting) in connection with the negotiation, administration, and valuation of the agreement; and
348	>
349	> • To the landowner\'s legal, financial, and tax advisors, in each case subject to obligations of confidentiality.
350	
351	**[XII.D. Right of First Refusal (ROFR)]{.underline}**
352	
353	Ridgeline holds a **right of first refusal** if the landowner receives a bona fide written offer from a third party to purchase all or any portion of the optioned or leased premises during the option period or lease term. The landowner must promptly deliver to Ridgeline a copy of the third-party offer together with all material terms. Ridgeline has **forty-five (45) days** from receipt of such notice to elect, by written notice, to match the terms of the third-party offer and purchase the property on substantially the same terms. If Ridgeline does not exercise its ROFR within the 45-day period, the landowner may proceed with the third-party sale, subject to the purchaser\'s assumption of the agreement.
354	
355	**[XII.E. Force Majeure]{.underline}**
356	
357	Neither party shall be in default for any failure or delay in performing its obligations under the agreement (other than the obligation to make monetary payments) to the extent such failure or delay is caused by events beyond the reasonable control of the affected party, including: epidemics and pandemics; orders, directives, or regulations of governmental authorities; supply chain disruptions; acts of God (including earthquakes, floods, wildfire, and severe weather events); war; terrorism; civil unrest; and labor disputes (including strikes and lockouts).
358	
359	Force majeure events toll the affected party\'s performance obligations for the duration of the event but do not excuse or defer monetary payment obligations (including option payments, rent, and Substation Hosting Fees).
360	
361	**[XIII. Deviation Tracking and Approval Process]{.underline}**
362	
363	Any executed agreement that deviates from a provision identified in this Playbook as a \"must-have\" or that falls outside the acceptable negotiation ranges set forth herein must be documented in **Ridgeline\'s Deviation Tracker** (maintained by the Legal Department) and approved in writing by Jordan Hale, VP of Land & Development, or Ridgeline\'s General Counsel.
364	
365	**Common Deviations Requiring Escalation and Approval:**
366	
367	1\. Decommissioning security posting obligation deferred beyond COD + 10 years.
368	
369	2\. Omission of the Qualified Transferee provision from the assignment clause.
370	
371	3\. Inclusion of mutual specific performance (acceptable but requires documentation of rationale and approval).
372	
373	4\. Rent calculation structure that does not clearly separate the Substation Hosting Fee from the greater-of comparison.
374	
375	5\. Absence of an MFN clause where the project involves five (5) or more landowner agreements.
376	
377	6\. Modification of assignment consent thresholds below the Qualified Transferee levels (\$50 million net worth / 200 MW operating experience).
378	
379	Land agents at Trailhead Land Services LLC (Kevin Obermeyer, Senior Land Agent) are responsible for flagging deviations to Ridgeline\'s legal team promptly upon identification --- whether the deviation arises during negotiation or is discovered during post-execution review of an agreement. Outside counsel (Westbrook Callahan LLP, Sarah Fong, Partner) should be consulted on any legal enforceability concerns arising from deviations, including but not limited to unconscionability, compliance with Oregon landlord-tenant law, and project finance lender covenant compliance.
380	
381	All approved deviations must include a written explanation of the business rationale and any compensating terms negotiated in exchange for the deviation.
382	
383	**[XIV. Contacts and Resources]{.underline}**
384	
385	The following individuals and entities are the primary contacts for questions, escalation, and coordination relating to land option and lease agreements under this Playbook:
386	
387	**Ridgeline Wind Holdings LLC** (Developer)

389	> Jordan Hale, VP of Land & Development 2200 SW Morrison Street, Suite 1400 Portland, OR 97205
390	
391	**Westbrook Callahan LLP** (Outside Counsel)

393	> Sarah Fong, Partner 900 SW Fifth Avenue, Suite 2600 Portland, OR 97204
394	
395	**Stratton Whitaker LLP** (Lender\'s Counsel)

400	
401	> Kevin Obermeyer, Senior Land Agent Pendleton, OR

408

410	
411	**Pineridge Surety Co.** (Surety Bond Provider)
412	
413	*End of Playbook --- Version 3.2 (Revised October 2024)*
414

issue(1,'No Lender Protections; Collateral Assignment Not Clearly Permitted','Critical',[
 ('Agreement.','Article 14 permits free assignment only to Affiliates (14.1) and Qualified Transferees (14.3); any other assignment of \"all or any portion\" of Developer\'s rights requires Landowner consent, not to be unreasonably withheld (14.2). There is no provision addressing collateral assignment, leasehold mortgages, lender notice and cure, step-in, new-lease rights following termination or rejection in bankruptcy, protection against amendment/surrender without lender consent, or estoppel certificates. Section 17.2 allows the Landowner to terminate on an uncured Developer default with no lender notice. Section 10.4\'s reference to lenders points only to Article 18, which is a confidentiality carve-out, not a lender-protection article.'),
 ('Why it matters.','Highline is a lender, not a wind owner/operator, and so very likely fails the 200 MW experience prong of Section 14.3(b); a collateral assignment or leasehold deed of trust is therefore arguably an \"assignment\" requiring consent under 14.2. Even with consent, a Landowner termination for an uncured Ridgeline default would extinguish Highline\'s collateral, including the only viable substation site. A foreclosure purchaser or lender designee also may not qualify as a Qualified Transferee. The Lender Checklist (Items 6 and 7) requires confirmation of collateral-assignment rights, simultaneous default notices to the lender and a separate lender cure period of at least 30 days beyond Ridgeline\'s cure period.  ('Playbook.','The Playbook does not contain a lender-protection must-have, but repeatedly identifies Highline financing as the purpose of key terms (IV.B personal property; VII.B; VIII). The omission is a gap rather than a negotiated deviation.')],
 ['Add a Lender Protection article in the First Amendment: (i) express right to mortgage/collaterally assign the leasehold and easements without consent; (ii) Landowner copies of default notices to each lender; (iii) lender cure period of at least 30 days beyond Ridgeline\'s (monetary) and 60+ days plus time to obtain possession/foreclose (non-monetary), with non-curable personal defaults waived for the lender; (iv) right of lender (or designee/foreclosure purchaser) to assume without consent, and to assign onward to a Qualified Transferee; (v) new-lease right on termination or bankruptcy rejection; (vi) no amendment, surrender or voluntary termination without lender consent; (vii) estoppel certificates within 10-15 business days on request; (viii) lender not personally liable until it takes possession; (ix) the right to partition the lease into separate leases/easements for financing.',

issue(3,'Section 4.1: Articles 5-19 Effective Only on Exercise','Critical',[
 ('Agreement.','Section 4.1 provides that \"[u]pon exercise of the Option, the lease provisions of this Agreement set forth in Articles 5 through 19 shall become effective as of the date of the Exercise Notice.\" Articles 5-19 include the representations (Art. 9), insurance (10), indemnity (11), taxes/personal property (12), decommissioning (13), assignment, Landowner transfer restriction and Memorandum (14), ROFR (15), defaults and remedies including specific performance (16), termination including Developer\'s Option-Period termination right (17.1), confidentiality (18) and arbitration (19).'),
 ('Conflict.','Several of those provisions expressly operate \"during the Option Period\" (14.4, 15.1, 17.1) or from the Effective Date (9.1/9.2 reps, 10.4 certificates within 30 days of the Effective Date, 14.5 recording \"promptly following the Effective Date\").  ('Why it matters.','Under ORS Chapter 93, an unrecorded interest is vulnerable to a subsequent bona fide purchaser or encumbrancer for value. Have Eleanor Millard (Trustee) and Jordan Hale sign and acknowledge; record in Gilliam County.',
  'Order the legal descriptions and attach a completed Exhibit A by amendment; attach the recorded memorandum as Exhibit B.',
  'Obtain a fully executed and acknowledged counterpart for the file and the Lender.'])

 ('Facts.','Per the Comps, Millard has the highest option rates ($18/$20/$22/$24), base rent ($1,200, tied with L002), capacity payment ($4,800) and royalty (3.5%) in the project.  [])

for k,v in [('Confidentiality conflict.','Section 18.1 does not permit disclosure of Millard terms to other landowners except \"as required by applicable law.\" Notifying MFN holders of the Millard terms could breach Section 18.1 unless the MFN true-up can be implemented without identifying Millard\'s terms, or the Trust consents.'),

 ('Agreement.','Section 4.1 provides that \"[u]pon exercise of the Option, the lease provisions of this Agreement set forth in Articles 5 through 19 shall become effective as of the date of the Exercise Notice.\" Articles 5-19 include the representations (Art. 9), insurance (10), indemnity (11), taxes/personal property (12), decommissioning (13), assignment, Landowner transfer restriction and Memorandum (14), ROFR (15), defaults and remedies including specific performance (16), termination including Developer\'s Option-Period termination right (17.1), confidentiality (18) and arbitration (19).'),
 ('Conflict.','Several of those provisions expressly operate \"during the Option Period\" (14.4, 15.1, 17.1) or from the Effective Date (9.1/9.2 reps, 10.4 certificates within 30 days of the Effective Date, 14.5 recording \"promptly following the Effective Date\"). A court would likely harmonize the specific provisions over the general Section 4.1 statement, but a Landowner (or a competing developer or purchaser) could argue that during the Option Period Ridgeline has no enforceable transfer restriction, ROFR, specific performance remedy or arbitration clause, and no confidentiality protection. This is exactly the period in which the Project Memo identifies the greatest site-control risk. It also means no insurance or indemnity is clearly required for the pre-development activities and met towers under Section 3.4.')],
 ['Amend Section 4.1 so that only the leasehold grant and lease economics (Arts. 5-8 and 13) commence on exercise, and Articles 9-12 and 14-21 apply from the Effective Date.',
  'Add an Option-Period insurance and indemnity requirement covering Section 3.4 activities (e.g., CGL $2-5M; landowner additional insured).'])

issue(4,'Incomplete Exhibits, Execution Formalities and Unconfirmed Recording','Critical',[
 ('Agreement.','Exhibit A contains only tax-lot references with metes-and-bounds descriptions \"to be provided\" by Columbia Basin Title & Escrow. Exhibit B is a bracketed placeholder, not a form. Section 14.5 requires prompt recording of a memorandum \"substantially in the form of Exhibit B\" - there is no form to conform to. The copy in our file has blank signature lines and incomplete notarial acknowledgments; the Lender says it received an \"executed copy\" (we should confirm it is the same version).'),
 ('Why it matters.','Under ORS Chapter 93, an unrecorded interest is vulnerable to a subsequent bona fide purchaser or encumbrancer for value. The Playbook (VI.B, XII.B) requires the memorandum to be executed simultaneously with the Agreement, to include a legally sufficient description and all material rights (option, lease, renewal, easements, ROFR), and to omit financial terms. Recording is a Lender priority item (Item 1, due January 24, 2025) and a condition precedent under Highline\'s draft credit agreement; a leasehold title policy will be required on exercise (Item 2). Oregon recording also requires an acknowledged instrument, so the notarial blocks must be completed.')],
 ['Confirm immediately with Jordan Hale and Columbia Basin Title & Escrow whether a memorandum has been recorded; if so obtain recording data (book/page or instrument number and date).',
  'If not, prepare a Memorandum of Option, Lease and Easement now: parties; Property by full legal description for all three tax lots; Option Period (to Dec. 18, 2027, extendable to Dec. 18, 2029); 30-yr Lease Term from COD plus 20-yr renewal; transmission easement; exclusivity; ROFR; Landowner transfer restriction; no financial terms. Have Eleanor Millard (Trustee) and Jordan Hale sign and acknowledge; record in Gilliam County.',
  'Order the legal descriptions and attach a completed Exhibit A by amendment; attach the recorded memorandum as Exhibit B.',
  'Obtain a fully executed and acknowledged counterpart for the file and the Lender.'])

issue(5,'MFN Cascade Created by Millard Terms; No MFN in Millard Agreement','Critical',[
 ('Facts.','Per the Comps, Millard has the highest option rates ($18/$20/$22/$24), base rent ($1,200, tied with L002), capacity payment ($4,800) and royalty (3.5%) in the project. MFN clauses are in L001, L003, L005 and L006 and in 9 of the 14 prior project agreements; per Comps they are \"typically triggered by any new agreement executed after the relevant agreement\'s date.\" Millard (executed Dec. 18, 2024) post-dates them all.'),
 ('Estimated exposure (four comparables only; Playbook-scope MFN assumed).','')],
 [])
rows = [
 ('APW-L001 Hargrove (lease active; ~45 MW)','+$2,000 (20 x $100)','+$13,500 (45 x $300)','3.0% -> 3.5%','N/A (exercised)'),
 ('APW-L003 Stenger Trust (~35 MW)','+$750 (15 x $50)','+$7,000 (35 x $200)','3.25% -> 3.5%','+$2,670/yr (1,780 ac x $1.50)'),
 ('APW-L005 Pryor Creek (~65 MW)','+$1,400 (28 x $50)','+$9,750 (65 x $150)','3.25% -> 3.5%','+$3,200/yr (3,200 ac x $1.00)'),
 ('APW-L006 Ridgeview (~55 MW)','+$600 (24 x $25)','+$5,500 (55 x $100)','3.25% -> 3.5%','+$1,235/yr (2,470 ac x $0.50)'),
 ('Total (4 agreements)','+$4,750/yr','+$35,750/yr','0.25-0.50 pts','~+$7,105/yr'),
]
T(['Agreement','Base rent (min. turbines)','Capacity payment (est. MW)','Royalty','Option rate uplift'], rows, widths=[1.9,1.3,1.4,1.0,1.4])
P('Fixed-rent uplift totals approximately **$40,500 per year** before the 2% escalator, i.e., on the order of $1.2 million+ undiscounted over a 30-year term before escalation, plus royalty uplift in years the royalty prong governs and the five unquantified MFN agreements outside the Comps. Estimates use Comps MW estimates and minimum turbine counts and must be verified against each MFN clause.', size=9.5)
for k,v in [('Confidentiality conflict.','Section 18.1 does not permit disclosure of Millard terms to other landowners except \"as required by applicable law.\" Notifying MFN holders of the Millard terms could breach Section 18.1 unless the MFN true-up can be implemented without identifying Millard\'s terms, or the Trust consents.'),
 ('No MFN for Millard.','Playbook XIII.5 requires escalation and documentation where an MFN is absent and the project has five or more landowner agreements. The Comps note the omission \"despite trust structure similar to APW-L003 (Stenger) which has MFN.\" Practical risk is currently low (Millard has the best terms), but rises if later agreements (the Lender references 15 agreements) or MFN true-ups produce better terms elsewhere.')]:

for r in ['Pull and review the MFN clauses in all nine MFN agreements (scope of terms covered, look-back, notice obligations, whether a \"package\" comparison or substation-fee carve-out applies, cure mechanics) and quantify exposure before financial close; Highline\'s pro forma (which the Project Memo says depends on Millard production) should reflect the result.',
 'Evaluate whether the Millard substation-hosting and parcel-specific characteristics support a position that the Millard package is not \"more favorable\" on a like-for-like basis; the Playbook MFN scope excludes Substation Hosting Fees and parcel-specific accommodations but includes per-turbine, per-MW, royalty and option rates.',
 'Seek Trust consent (in the First Amendment) to disclose terms as needed to satisfy MFN obligations in other project agreements.',

    B(r)

H('B. High-Priority Issues', 2)
issue(6,'Option Exercise Strategy, Extension Deadline Error and Year 4 Payment Question','High',[
 ('Deadline error.','Section 3.2 requires notice \"not less than ninety (90) days prior to the expiration\" of the current period and then states that \"[a]ccordingly\" the deadlines are September 20, 2027 and September 20, 2028. The initial Option Period expires at 11:59 p.m. PT on Saturday, December 18, 2027; September 20, 2027 is only 89 days earlier. Ninety days before December 18 is **Sunday, September 19, 2027** (and **Tuesday, September 19, 2028** for the second extension). The Agreement has no business-day roll-forward. The Project Memo and Playbook repeat the September 20 date. A Landowner could argue a September 20 notice is untimely under the 90-day formula; failure of timely notice causes the Option to lapse (Sec. 3.2). Notice by certified mail is deemed delivered only 3 business days after deposit (Art. 20).'),
 ('Date misalignment.','Section 3.1 defines the First Extension Period as Dec. 19, 2027-Dec. 18, 2028, while the payment table in Section 3.3 runs Extension Year 4 from Dec. 18, 2027-Dec. 17, 2028 (and the Year 4 payment is due \"on or before\" Dec. 18, 2027 - the last day of the initial period). Harmless if Ridgeline pays early, but it should be conformed.'),
 ('Exercise timing - the Project Memo\'s premise needs correcting.','The Project Memo assumes Ridgeline would \"exercise the option and convert to the lease upon achieving COD.\" That is not how the Agreement works. Section 3.4 pre-development rights are limited to studies and met towers; construction rights (Art. 7), the transmission easement (7.2) and the leasehold arise only upon exercise (4.1). The Project Memo schedule contemplates financial close in Q2 2026 and road/foundation construction beginning Q3 2026, and the Lender will require a leasehold title policy on exercise. Ridgeline therefore must exercise **before construction begins and, practically, at or before financial close** - i.e., more than a year before the September 2027 extension deadline. Once exercised, the Lease Term runs from COD (5.1) and the Construction Period (5.3) has no outside date, so a COD slip past December 18, 2027 does not forfeit site control. The extension decision is relevant only if exercise is delayed beyond the planned construction start.'),
 ('Project Memo question 1 - exercise after an extension notice.','Yes. Section 3.2 expressly provides that \"[n]o extension election shall affect or modify Developer\'s right to exercise the Option at any time during the then-current Option Period or Extension Period,\" and Section 4.1 permits exercise at any time during the Option Period \"including any Extension Period.\" Exercise is effective on delivery of the Exercise Notice.'),
 ('Project Memo question 2 - Year 4 payment.','The Agreement does not answer this cleanly. Option Payments are payable in advance on or before each anniversary (3.3) and an extension notice is irrevocable (3.2), so a Landowner could claim the full $92,400 Year 4 payment once an extension notice is delivered. However, once the Option is exercised Section 5.3 replaces annual Option Payments with the \"applicable Option Payment rate on a pro rata basis\" until COD. If Ridgeline exercises before Dec. 18, 2027 and COD occurs before that date, the better reading is that no Year 4 payment is owed; if COD has not occurred by Dec. 18, 2027, Ridgeline will owe pro rata Construction Period payments at the Year 4 rate ($22/acre, ~$253/day) in any event. The Agreement also does not say whether a full-year Option Payment prepaid before exercise is credited against Section 5.3 pro rata payments, creating double-payment risk for the year of exercise.')],
 ['Calendar the extension deadline as **Friday, September 17, 2027** (last business day before the Sunday 90-day date) with internal target of August 2, 2027, using personal delivery or overnight courier; similarly September 19, 2028 (target August 2028).',
  'Plan to deliver the Exercise Notice at or before financial close (Q2 2026) and in all events before construction starts; the Exercise Notice must identify the intended construction commencement date (4.1).',
  'In the First Amendment: conform the deadline dates to the 90-day formula (or restate as a fixed date of Sept. 17); align the period dates; clarify that exercise terminates any remaining Option Payment obligation other than Section 5.3 pro rata payments and credits any prepaid Option Payment; state a Construction Period rate after Dec. 17, 2029; and consider extending the Option Period day-for-day for force majeure and permitting/interconnection delays (currently no tolling).',
  'Correct the Project Memo\'s recommendations in the response to the client (see Part V).'])

issue(7,'Substation Hosting Fee Not Expressly \"In Addition To\" Lease Rent','High',[
 ('Agreement.','Section 6.5 sets a $35,000/yr Substation Fee in a separate section and Section 6.4 defines \"Lease Rent\" as the greater of prong (a) or (b). Section 6.5 says \"Developer shall pay\" the fee but does not state that it is payable in addition to Lease Rent regardless of which prong applies, or that it is excluded from the comparison. The Comps flag the same issue (\"not explicitly included in prong (a) or (b)\"; note that the Comps cite \"Section 5.4\" and \"Section 5.1,\" which are incorrect - the provisions are Sections 6.5 and 6.4).'),
 ('Playbook.','III.B labels this CRITICAL and requires language substantially similar to the model clause; omission is a listed deviation requiring approval (XIII.4). The Playbook notes this ambiguity has caused disputes in prior negotiations. The structure of Article 6 makes the better reading favorable (the fee is separate consideration for a distinct use), but the Playbook standard is unambiguous language.')],
 ['Insert the Playbook model language in Section 6.5 via the First Amendment (\"In addition to the Lease Rent calculated under Section 6.4 ... shall not be included in either prong for purposes of the greater-of comparison\").',
  'Log as a deviation pending amendment.'])

issue(8,'Indemnity Survival and Environmental Insurance Tail','High',[
 ('Agreement.','Article 11 indemnities survive 3 years after expiration or termination (11.3). Environmental insurance ($2M per occurrence) is required only through the Lease Term and any Renewal Term (10.3) - not during the Option Period and not after expiration while latent claims may surface. Decommissioning (up to 18 months) and restoration certification can extend well past expiration.'),
 ('Benchmarks.','Playbook IX accepts 3 years but flags that ORS 12.080 allows 6 years for property-damage claims and ORS 12.110 applies a discovery-based 2-year period for personal injury, and suggests 5-6 years for environmentally sensitive sites. L001, L002, L003 and L006 provide 5 years; L004/L005 provide 3. Highline (Item 4) will likely require an extended survival period or environmental coverage coterminous with limitation periods.'),
 ('Scope summary for Lender Item 4.','(a) Scope: Developer indemnifies Landowner, Trustee, Successor Trustee, beneficiaries, agents, heirs and assigns for Developer\'s activities (construction through decommissioning), bodily injury/death related to the Facilities, and environmental contamination caused by the Facilities, including defense and reasonable attorneys\' fees (11.1). (b) Carve-out: Landowner Indemnified Parties\' gross negligence or willful misconduct; no cap; no exclusion of consequential damages in the indemnity. Reciprocal Landowner indemnity for non-project use, excluding Developer\'s negligence (11.2). (c) Survival: 3 years (11.3).')],
 ['Extend survival to 6 years (aligned with ORS 12.080), or alternatively to the later of 6 years and completion of decommissioning/restoration certification under Section 13.2, at least for environmental claims.',
  'Require environmental coverage (or an extended reporting period/tail) for the survival period and add Option-Period coverage.',
  'This is landowner-favorable and can be offered as part of the amendment package.'])

issue(9,'Asymmetric Remedies - Enforceability Risk','High',[
 ('Agreement.','Developer receives specific performance and injunctive relief without proof of damages or bond, plus monetary damages \"including consequential damages\" (16.2). Landowner\'s exclusive remedies are termination and direct damages; no specific performance or injunction \"under any circumstances\" (16.3).'),
 ('Risk.','This tracks the Playbook preferred position (X.B), but the Playbook itself warns that Oregon courts may decline to enforce one-sided remedy limitations deemed unconscionable where there is a disparity in bargaining power, particularly for an elderly individual or trust fiduciary. Here: the Trustee is 74; the Agreement contains no acknowledgment of independent counsel (contrast Stenger Trust, L003, whose \"[t]rustee [was] represented by independent counsel\"); there is no MFN; and L001, L003 and L006 grant mutual specific performance. The asymmetry is compounded by consequential damages flowing only to Ridgeline. Because Ridgeline\'s specific-performance right is what protects the irreplaceable substation site, a successful unconscionability challenge would undercut the provision Ridgeline most needs. The Lender has not yet raised this, but lender\'s counsel may.')],
 ['Do not concede without consulting you (Playbook X.B).',
  'In the First Amendment, consider adding an acknowledgment that the Trust was advised to and had the opportunity to obtain independent counsel, and confirming whether Trust counsel was involved.',
  'Consider making consequential-damages waivers mutual (or excluding lost profits on both sides) as a low-cost fairness improvement that strengthens enforceability of Section 16.2.'])

issue(10,'Insurance Provisions vs. Playbook Must-Have and Lender Item 5','High',[
 ('Agreement.','Limits match the Playbook and the Lender list exactly (construction CGL $5M/$10M, umbrella $25M; operations CGL $3M/$5M, umbrella $15M; environmental $2M). However: (i) no covenant to give 30 days\' notice of cancellation, non-renewal or material modification (a Playbook VIII must-have); (ii) certificates are tied to the Effective Date and anniversaries rather than policy inception/renewal, and are delivered to lenders only \"upon request\"; (iii) Highline is not required to be named as additional insured (Lender Item 5); (iv) no insurance is required during the Option Period although certificates are due within 30 days of the Effective Date - it is unclear what coverage those certificates evidence; (v) the A- (VII) rating requirement applies only to construction policies.')],
 ['Confirm what pre-construction liability coverage is in place for met tower and survey work and whether certificates were delivered by January 17, 2025 (30 days after the Effective Date).',
  'Amend Article 10 to add the cancellation-notice covenant, lender additional-insured/loss-payee status, inception/renewal delivery, rating requirement for all policies, and Option-Period coverage.'])

issue(11,'Trust Authority and Landowner Succession','High',[
 ('Agreement.','The Trust represents that Eleanor Millard as Trustee may bind the trust without beneficiary, co-trustee or court consent (9.2(b)) and that it holds fee title (9.2(c)). Permitted Landowner transfers are limited to transfers among trust beneficiaries and to a successor trustee (14.4); there is no exception for transfers by operation of law, inheritance or court order, or subordinate refinancing, all of which the Playbook VI.B lists as permitted.'),
 ('Risk.','Given the Trustee\'s age and a 50+ year term, the Lender and title insurer will require evidence of trustee authority and succession. A revocable trust may become irrevocable or be divided on the settlor\'s death; transfers by operation of law that fall outside 14.4 would technically require Ridgeline\'s consent in its sole discretion, which a court could view as an unreasonable restraint on alienation. The 14.4 exceptions also do not expressly require transferees to take subject to the ROFR.')],
 ['Obtain a certification of trust (ORS 130.860) and relevant trust excerpts confirming Eleanor Millard\'s sole trustee powers and Douglas Millard\'s successor status; have Douglas Millard countersign an acknowledgment of the Agreement.',
  'Conform Section 14.4 to Playbook VI.B (operation-of-law transfers; refinancing subordinate to or recognizing the Memorandum), with every transferee bound to the Agreement.',
  'Obtain the Developer-side managing-member resolution referenced in Section 9.1(c) for the Lender package.'])
EOF
echo ok"
